sahneler.metin: A wave of molasses tore through Boston at thirty five miles an hour.
It crushed buildings and killed twenty one people.
So how did a storage tank do that?
It was built in a rush, with no engineer checking it.
The steel was too thin and too brittle for cold.
It leaked from day one, so the company painted it brown.
A warm spell raised the pressure until the rivets tore open.
Massachusetts then made engineer sign-off the law.

aciklama:
On January 15, 1919, a molasses storage tank in Boston burst, releasing a wave that killed 21 people. The tank had never been inspected by an engineer.

#shorts #engineering #history
